newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Telekom eyes raising cellular mkt share.
newsitem.headline: Telekom eyes raising cellular mkt share.

text.p: Telekom Malaysia Bhd said on Tuesday it aims to raise the subscriber base of a newly-acquired cellular phone company to 100,000 in 1997 from 17,000.

The 100,000 target for wholly-owned Telekom Cellular Sdn Bhd amounts to a market share of six to seven percent, Telekom's chief executive Mohamed Said Mohamed Ali was quoted as saying by the national Bernama news agency.
Telekom Cellular, formerly MRCB Telecommunications Sdn Bhd, was bought from Malaysian Resources Corp Bhd for 635 million ringgit.
Mohamed Said, who relaunched the phone company on Tuesday, said he expected Telekom Cellular to break even by 1999.
Telekom Cellular's network has been renamed TMTouch. The network was called Emartel when it was operated by MRCB Telecommunications.
Telekom said it would invest at least 500 million ringgit over the next three years to upgrade the network, which runs on the Global System for Mobile Systems (GSM), said Mohamed Said.
Telekom Cellular is Telekom's third cellular phone operation. Telekom has a 30 percent stake in Mobikom Sdn Bhd and wholly-owned the Atur 450 service.
Mohamed Said said the company was still considering whether to combine all the three mobile phone businesses, Bernama said.
